text: Sing for joy in the LORD, you righteous; praise is fitting for the upright.
Give thanks to the LORD with the harp; make music to him on the ten-stringed lyre.
Sing him a new song; play skillfully, with a shout of joy.
For the word of the LORD is right, and all his work is done in faithfulness.
He loves righteousness and justice; the earth is full of the steadfast love of the LORD.
By the word of the LORD the heavens were made, and all their host by the breath of his mouth.
He gathers the waters of the sea as in a heap; he puts the deeps into storehouses.
Let all the earth fear the LORD; let all who live in the world stand in awe of him.
For he spoke, and it came to be; he commanded, and there it stood.
The LORD overturns the plans of the nations; he thwarts the schemes of the peoples.
The counsel of the LORD stands forever, the thoughts of his heart through all generations.
Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD, the people he chose as his own inheritance.
From heaven the LORD looks down and sees all the sons of Adam.

versions.text: From heaven the LORD looks down and sees all the children of men.
versions.explanation: "Children of men" is dated and gendered in an unclear way for oral reading; "all humankind" or "all the sons of Adam" better renders בְּנֵי הָאָדָם. Either is acceptable; consider "all humankind" for smoother flow.

text: From his throne where he sits enthroned he gazes on all who dwell on the earth—

versions.text: From his dwelling place he watches all who live on the earth—
versions.explanation: מְכוֹן שִׁבְתּוֹ denotes the fixed place of his enthronement; "dwelling place" loses the royal nuance. Optionally: "From his royal seat he gazes on all who dwell on the earth—".

text: he who forms the hearts of them all, who understands everything they do.
No king is saved by the greatness of his army; no warrior is delivered by his great strength.

versions.text: No king is saved by the size of his army; no warrior escapes by his great strength.
versions.explanation: The parallelism in Hebrew uses רָב twice ("greatness/abundance"); matching the wording strengthens the oral parallelism, and יִנָּצֵל is passive ("is delivered") rather than "escapes."

text: The horse is a false hope for deliverance; for all its great strength it cannot save.

versions.text: A horse is a false hope for victory; for all its power it cannot deliver.
versions.explanation: תְּשׁוּעָה here means deliverance/salvation, echoing נוֹשָׁע in v.16; also חַיִל repeats from v.16 and should be echoed for the parallel.

text: But the eye of the LORD is on those who fear him, on those who hope in his steadfast love,
to rescue their souls from death and keep them alive in famine.
Our soul waits for the LORD; he is our help and our shield.

versions.text: We wait for the LORD; he is our help and our shield.
versions.explanation: נַפְשֵׁנוּ ("our soul") is dropped; retaining it preserves the parallel with נַפְשָׁם in v.19 and the personal depth of the line.

text: In him our heart rejoices, for we trust in his holy name.
Let your steadfast love rest on us, LORD, even as we put our hope in you.
